# 4-Day Lisbon Trip Plan from Toronto

A relaxed Lisbon plan for 2 adults with museums, walking, seafood, and one half-day free. I’m assuming you want the trip centered on Lisbon city, with a central 3-star or boutique hotel and economy-to-premium-economy flights if available.

## Trip Itinerary and Cost Plan

### Day 1: Arrival + Baixa/Chiado Intro
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Fly Toronto to Lisbon; arrive and check in near Baixa, Chiado, or Rossio.
- Afternoon: Gentle walk through Baixa, Rossio, and Praça do Comércio; keep this light after travel.
- Dinner: Seafood rice or grilled sardines at a central tascas-style restaurant.
- Pace: Easy first day, minimal transit.

### Day 2: Alfama, Cathedral, and Fado-Style Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Self-guided walk in Alfama; stop at Lisbon Cathedral and viewpoints.
- Afternoon: Visit a museum in the historic core, such as Museu do Fado or a nearby art/history museum.
- Dinner: Seafood-focused dinner in Alfama or Chiado; book ahead if you want a nicer place.
- Pace: Moderate walking, lots of scenic pauses.

### Day 3: Belém Museums + Half-Day Free
- Morning: Head to Belém for one major museum or monument, plus a riverside walk.
- Afternoon: Free half-day for rest, café time, souvenir browsing, or a second museum if energy is good.
- Dinner: Casual seafood dinner back in central Lisbon.
- Pace: Built-in downtime, low stress.

### Day 4: Final Stroll + Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- Morning: Short final walk in the city center, coffee, and last photos.
- Afternoon: Check out and transfer to the airport.
- Dinner: In transit or airport meal depending on flight time.
- Pace: Keep the morning flexible for departure timing.

## Estimated Budget for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimate (CAD) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Flights Toronto ↔ Lisbon | 1,300–1,800 | Best chance of staying on budget if booked early |
| Hotel, 3 nights | 450–540 | Targeting under CAD 180/night before taxes/fees |
| Local transport | 60–120 | Metro, tram, taxi/ride-hail, airport transfer |
| Food and drinks | 650–900 | Mix of cafés, seafood dinners, and simple lunches |
| Attractions and museums | 120–220 | Museum entries, optional guided walk, viewpoints |
| Buffer | 200–300 | Small overruns, transit, coffee, extras |
| Total | 2,780–3,880 | Best-fit target: **CAD 3,000–3,200** with careful flight/hotel pricing |

### Cost Fit
- **Most likely to stay within budget:** midweek flights, central 3-star hotel, 1–2 nicer seafood dinners, mostly self-guided walking.
- **Likely budget pressure points:** flights and hotel taxes/fees.
- **Best savings lever:** choose a hotel just outside the most premium core of Chiado, while staying walkable to Rossio/Baixa.

## Packing Checklist for Lisbon in September

### Essentials
- Passport, travel insurance, flight and hotel confirmations
- Wallet with 2 payment cards and some backup cash
- Phone charger, power bank, and EU plug adapter
- Copies of key documents stored digitally

### Clothing
- Light layers for warm days and cooler evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- One nicer outfit for dinner
- Compact rain layer or small umbrella

### City-Trip Extras
- Sunglasses, sunscreen, and reusable water bottle
- Small day bag or crossbody bag for museum days
- Light scarf or wrap for churches and cooler evenings
- Earplugs or sleep mask for the flight

### Nice-to-Have Items
- Portable laundry soap sheets for a short trip
- Motion sickness tablets if you are sensitive on trams or taxis
- A small notebook for restaurant and museum notes

## Quick Actions
